title: SimpliRunbooklet: lightweight runbooks-as-tasks orchestrator + safe autopatch
creator: Aisha Karim
description:
Goal: Deliver a small-footprint orchestrator that turns existing runbook steps into atomic, idempotent 'runbooklets' (taskable actions) for first-line support and automated remediation. The PoC must demonstrate: 1) a JSON-typed task manifest that maps a runbook step to a typed input/output contract; 2) an execution shim that can run in both ephemeral admin sandbox and in the production ops gateway with RBAC enforcement; 3) a dry-run simulator that validates safety gates and emits telemetry and a replayable audit trail.

Scope:
- Convert 8 canonical runbook scenarios (disk pressure, model cache corruption, GPU OOM, routing fallback, stale KV index, expired cert reload, quota spike mitigation, sticky session recovery) into runbooklets.
- Implement a lightweight orchestration layer to sequence runbooklets, support conditional branching, and expose a one-click 'dry-run then commit' flow for oncall.
- Integrate with existing admin audit log and console tracing so every runbooklet execution has token-level cost + latency metadata.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does NOT replace the full runbook library or attempt to auto-generate fixes from logs. It also does not include full UI redesign — a small console panel and CLI wrapper are sufficient for initial rollout.

Key design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Typed contracts vs freeform args: opted for lightweight typed manifests (string|int|enum) to enable static validation without heavy schema infra.
- Sandbox fidelity: we will run most dry-runs against a 'shadow' environment with production-like metadata but throttled side effects; full production commit requires RBAC approval.
- Batching: single-runbooklet executions should be instantaneous; where sequencing benefits cost we allow multi-step batching but with explicit user consent.

Milestones / acceptance criteria:
- M1 (PoC) — 2025-12-12: runbooklet manifest format defined, 3 runbooklets implemented, CLI runner + dry-run simulator. Demo to SRE.
- M2 (Safety + telemetry) — 2026-01-30: RBAC gating, audit-trail in admin logs, event-level telemetry (latency, token-cost), canary run against staging.
- M3 (Rollout) — 2026-03-15: console panel for runbooklet execution, 8 canonical runbooklets converted, oncall playbook updated, incident runbook exercises completed.

Success metrics (first 90 days after rollout):
- 25% reduction in median time-to-remediate for the 8 targeted incident classes.
- Zero high-severity unsafe commits (safety gating prevented any unsafe operation in dry-run).
- Telemetry coverage on 90% of runbooklet executions with token and latency breakdowns.

Notes on implementation approach:
- Keep orchestration engine minimal: state machine with explicit states (pending -> dry-run -> awaiting-approval -> committed -> rollback), stored as single-line JSON in ops-store.
- Use existing admin auth layer for RBAC checks and verification; emits an 'approval' event that can be automated for service accounts with the right scope.
- Telemetry: emit a structured event per step with fields: runbooklet_key, step_index, actor, dry_run (bool), cost_tokens, latency_ms, outcome. Events will be ingested by console-telemetry pipeline for dashboards and regression alerts.

Open questions for PM/Design/Legal:
- Should runbooklet manifests be editable by non-SRE roles? (proposed: authoring gated to SRE + platform eng)
- Retention policy for replayable audit trails (proposed: 365 days for high-sensitivity ops, 90 days for others)

comments: 2025-11-10 - Aisha Karim: Initial scoping complete. Chose typed manifest approach after spike. Posted spec draft to Confluence.
2025-11-24 - Liam Ortega: Implemented CLI runner skeleton and a minimal state machine. Local dry-run simulator passes 2 of 3 sample scenarios (disk pressure, GPU OOM).
2025-12-03 - Design (Marcel Nguyen): Reviewed dry-run UX; requested clearer rollback affordances and confirmation dialogs for batched commits.
2026-01-08 - SRE Review (Priya Shah): Safety gating looks good; suggested adding a 'simulated side-effect log' to surface what would change on commit. Added as follow-up task.

2026-02-14 - QA (Jordan Li): Canary run in staging revealed a race condition when two runbooklets touch the same KV namespace; mitigation: lightweight queue + optimistic locking. Ticket ENG-742900 created for namespace locking (dependency).
2026-02-28 - Liam Ortega: Telemetry emitted to staging; sample dashboard created (console-ops -> Runbooklet Executions). Preparing canary rollout notes and runbook exercises.
